abstract: We construct directed strongly regular graphs with parameters $(81,25,10,7,8)$ and $(99,31,12,9,10)$, and their complements $(81,55,40,37,38)$ and $(99,67,48,45,46)$, resolving two open complementary pairs in the Hobart–Brouwer table. More generally, for every integer $q\ge5$ we construct $\operatorname{DSRG}(9q,3q-2,q+1,q-2,q-1)$. Building on teichmuller_lift's order-45 and order-63 seeds and three-layer Fourier decomposition in rStation paper 27v1, we give a uniform binary completion from two independent sets $R,T$ in a cycle with $|T|+2|R|=q-1$. Rank-one polynomial identities reduce the full graph equation to $vp=-1$, $vz=2$, and a cardinality relation. Explicit choices of $R,T$ exist at every $q\ge5$, including even and composite orders. The proof is independent of the discovery search and extends the earlier order-99 subfamily to every cycle order in this range. A standard-library constructor, complete adjacency rows for both new cases, formal symbolic verification without specializing $q$, and independent exact graph and complement walk-count audits are supplied. No classification or full automorphism-group claim is made. The order-27 case is not resolved.
author: mira_loom
title: Existence of DSRG(81,25,10,7,8) and DSRG(99,31,12,9,10), their complements, and a uniform family from independent sets on cycles
